analysis_md:
# ERIC — Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson
v5 run, 2026-10-14. In scope (market cap $32.016B at $9.58, nasdaq_quote_api). IFRS filer (Form 20-F, reports in SEK); all USD figures are the engine's period-end ECB-rate conversions recorded in dcf_numbers.json.

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, or ttm.py output — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Swedish telecom equipment maker: radio access networks (RAN) and core networks sold to carriers, cloud software & services, and an enterprise segment built around Vonage (CPaaS, acquired 2022) and private networks. One of only two Western RAN suppliers (with Nokia). Revenue is carrier-capex driven and currently flat: Q2 2026 sales SEK 52.7B, −6% reported / −1% organic (lower IPR licensing after a one-off settlement in Q2 2025), adjusted gross margin 48.4%, adjusted EBITA SEK 6.9B (13.1% margin). Q3 2026 reports tomorrow (Oct 15, 2026); consensus expects a hard YoY comparison because Q3 2025 contained a large IPR settlement.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (20-F via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $3,578,145,320; capex $285,565,400; SBC $194,358,200 — by override, see OVERRIDE (SEK 1,790M from Note G3, converted at the 2025 period-end rate).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $3,098,221,720 = $0.9271/share**
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $3,384,767,380 — same ballpark, modestly above the conservative figure.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, but the path is violent: FY2023 conservative OE was only $208,143,100 because OCF collapsed to $714,757,430 that year (working-capital and restructuring outflows), vs $3,819,596,460 in FY2024.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base, median of last 3 FY OE/share = $0.9271/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The latest FY is itself the median year (FY2023 ≈ $0.06, FY2025 $0.9271, FY2024 above it), so the base is neither the trough nor the peak.
- **No TTM base:** STALE_FY fired (FY ended 9.4 months ago), but ttm.py reads us-gaap facts only and exited 3 for this IFRS filer: "ttm.py: cannot compute TTM for ERIC (CIK 717826): ocf: no annual (FY) fact; sbc: no annual (FY) fact; shares_diluted: no annual (FY) fact; capex: no capex facts in companyfacts under any candidate tag and no capex_override in judgment.json — refusing to zero-fill". Per the v5 method for IFRS names, the median base stands. The 2026 interim prints that are public (Q1/Q2 6-Ks: sales −6% reported in Q2, net income SEK 4.1B in Q2) give no evidence a TTM base would sit above the median base.
- Balance sheet: net debt −$1,546,504,940, i.e. **net cash** (net_debt_to_normalized_oe −0.50x, diagnostics). The dividend was raised to SEK 3.00/share and the company is running its first-ever buyback — up to SEK 15B through March 31, 2027 (SEK 872M repurchased in the Sep 28–Oct 2, 2026 week alone, per company disclosures reported by Yahoo Finance).

## OVERRIDE — sbc (filing-sourced, declared under bounded authority)
- **The gap:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:sbc — sbc missing for fiscal year(s) 2023, 2024, 2025 of the last 3`. Ericsson's ifrs-full tag `ExpenseFromSharebasedPaymentTransactionsWithEmployees` is filed only through FY2019 (SEK 256M); companyfacts carries no SBC for 2020–2025 under any candidate tag. (One trap avoided: the similarly named `ExpenseFromSharebasedPaymentTransactionsInWhichGoodsOrServicesReceivedDidNotQualifyForRecognitionAsAssets` — SEK 3,337M/4,257M/5,380M for 2023/24/25 — is NOT the annual expense: in the FY2025 20-F instance it is the cumulative column of Note G3's multi-year expense table plus its maturity breakdown, not a per-year flow. It was not used.)
- **The decision (worker, bounded authority, kind "filing"):** judgment.json carries `sbc_override = {value: 1790000000, kind: "filing", source: "Ericsson Form 20-F for FY2025 (filed 2026-03-12), Financial Report Note G3 'Share-based compensation', table 'Compensation expense for LTV 2022–2025': total compensation expense SEK 1,206M (2023), SEK 2,080M (2024), SEK 1,790M (2025)…"}`. The engine's single-value mechanics fill every untagged period (2020–2025) with SEK 1,790M, which is both the filed FY2025 figure and the median of the three filed gap-year figures, so the median-of-3 base is built from filed figures; the per-year error vs the filed 2023/2024 figures is ~1% of OE in opposite directions. Band check (dcf_numbers.json override_checks): value SEK 1,790M vs last filed SEK 256M = ~7.0×, out_of_band: false. The step-up from 2019 is real — the Key Contributor cash-settled plans scaled up from 2022 (Note G3). Composition matters for interpretation: ~90% of the expense is cash-settled plans (a genuine cash cost, paid through provisions — accumulated payouts over 2025 were SEK 1,590M per Note G3); only SEK 175M of FY2025's total is share-settled. The sweep's rule — SBC is always a real cost — is applied to the full filed expense.
- **Measured impact (dcf_numbers.json override_impact):** base OE/share $0.9852 zero-fill → $0.9271 with override (−5.9%); weighted IRR 13.27% → 12.64%. Tier C either way — the override's binding effect is that a tier exists at all (unblocks_tier), not the tier level.
- **ADS ratio (separate gate, same run):** judgment.json carries `ads_ratio = {ratio: 1.0, source: FY2025 20-F cover — "American Depositary Shares (each representing one B share)"}`. Per-share figures needed no scaling.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: one of only two Western RAN vendors with a top-tier cellular patent portfolio, deep carrier installed base and scale R&D — but RAN is a re-bid, capex-cycle product business with no end-customer lock-in, Huawei leads globally on price, the market is flat between 5G/6G cycles, and the Vonage excursion showed capital allocation can destroy the moat's earnings.
- FOR: one of two Western RAN suppliers (with Nokia); EU/US high-risk-vendor phase-outs structurally exclude Huawei/ZTE from much of its market; deep installed base with the world's largest carriers plus multi-year managed-services/software contracts — real switching friction in live networks; top-tier cellular SEP portfolio generating a high-margin IPR licensing annuity; scale R&D and standards leadership in 5G/early 6G that smaller vendors cannot match.
- AGAINST: RAN is a re-bid, price-competitive product business — carriers squeeze vendors and no end user is locked in; global RAN market flat between cycles, growth hostage to carrier capex timing (India rollouts, North America digestion); Huawei remains the global share leader and price aggressor outside restricted markets; IPR licensing income is lumpy and settlement-driven, and margins are exposed to component (memory) cost inflation not immediately passable to customers; Enterprise/Vonage capital allocation destroyed value — SEK 32B (2023) and SEK 15.1B (2024) impairments.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-14)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine's blended growth is +6.96% and its OE/share CAGR (2y) component is +284.76% — an artifact of OE recovering off the depressed FY2023 OCF year, not an operating growth rate. The revenue components say flat (−1.99% 5-yr CAGR, −0.44% 3-yr CAGR), and the +14.36% latest revenue YoY is a USD-translation artifact of SEK appreciation (period-end rate 0.09066 → 0.10858 in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion); in reporting currency, sales declined in FY2025 and Q2 2026 printed −6% reported / −1% organic. Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.12 / −0.10 / −0.05 / +0.01 / +0.05 vs g_base) to −5.1% / −3.1% / **+1.9%** / +7.9% / +11.9%. The base start of +1.9% sits modestly above current prints for one mechanical reason: the SEK 15B buyback (~5% of the share count over a year at current pace) accretes OE/share even with flat operating OE. Bull starts assume the EU high-risk-vendor phase-out and a 6G pre-cycle turn carrier capex up; super bear assumes the guided H2 2026 memory/component cost squeeze (management guided Q3 Networks gross margin to ~49%, from 50.4% in Q2) compounds with a capex downturn. Probabilities 10/30/30/20/10 — bear-tilted for a flat market with guided margin pressure; OE multipliers at defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $9.58.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −5.1% | 0.75 | Capex downturn + component-cost squeeze; IPR drought | $4.14 | 7.59% |
| Bear | 30% | −3.1% | 0.90 | Flat RAN, margin give-back, lumpy IPR stays low | $5.41 | 9.33% |
| Base | 30% | +1.9% | 1.00 | Flat operating OE, buyback accretion, margins hold near current levels | $7.41 | 12.15% |
| Bull | 20% | +7.9% | 1.10 | EU vendor phase-out share gains + 6G pre-cycle capex turn | $10.45 | 16.07% |
| Super bull | 10% | +11.9% | 1.25 | Full upcycle: share gains, Enterprise breakeven, IPR renewals at peak rates | $14.00 | 20.15% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $7.75 (−19.1% vs price), IV@12% $10.23 (+6.8%), IV@10% $12.99, weighted IRR 12.64%, base-case IRR 12.15%**
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 9.68%, terminal value 18.1% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.38x, net debt −0.50x normalized OE (net cash), 9.4 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:sbc** (preliminary run): resolved by the filing-sourced override — see OVERRIDE. The gap is recorded in dcf_numbers.json data_gap with data_gap_uncovered empty.
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9 months ago): ttm.py cannot run on an IFRS filer (exit 3, message quoted in Owner's earnings); the engine's median base is used per the v5 IFRS rule. Public 2026 interim prints (Q2 2026: sales −6% reported / −1% organic, adjusted EBITA margin 13.1%) are consistent with the flat base case, not with a higher TTM base.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share range >3x over 5 yrs): real and explained — FY2023 OCF collapsed on working-capital/restructuring outflows while FY2024–25 recovered. Handled by the median-of-3 base (which discards the trough year as the median input) plus 40% combined weight on bear/super-bear.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024): the one-offs are the Vonage impairments — 2023 net income −$2,599,697,360 was driven by the ~SEK 32B Vonage goodwill impairment (non-cash) while OCF stayed positive at $714,757,430; 2024 net income of only $33,906,840 against OCF of $4,194,022,260 reflects the further SEK 15.1B of mainly Vonage intangible impairments (named in the FY2025 20-F tax note). Because the base is OCF-derived, the impairments do not contaminate OE — but they are a real capital-allocation verdict and are counted in the moat AGAINST pillars.
- **FX_CONVERTED**: reporting currency SEK converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app); flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average — rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion (2025: 0.10858). Consequence watched: USD growth rates flatter the underlying business when SEK strengthens, which is exactly what the +14.36% latest revenue YoY does; scenario starts were set off reporting-currency reality instead.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED**: 20-F filer; ads_ratio 1.0 declared from the FY2025 20-F cover ("each representing one B share") — per-share figures are per ADS with no scaling.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc**: see OVERRIDE — gap, decision, source, band check and measured impact are all recorded in fields (judgment.json, dcf_numbers.json overrides_applied/override_impact), not just here.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The method range is narrow for once: zero-fill SBC (indefensible, but the bounding case) gives weighted IRR 13.27%; the filed-SBC run gives 12.64%. Both are Tier C. There is no defensible input set found in this run that clears 15% at $9.58 — even the bull case only reaches 16.07% IRR.
- What the price is paying for: at $9.58 the market is capitalizing the margin-recovery story (adjusted gross margin 48.4% and rising) plus buyback accretion, in a market Dell'Oro-style trackers expect to stay flat in 2026, with management itself guiding H2 margins down on memory costs. The Q3 print lands tomorrow (Oct 15) against a settlement-inflated comparison — a weak print is the priced risk, not a surprise.
- Quality is genuinely decent: net cash, OE yield 9.68% on the normalized base, capex only ~8% of OCF, a raised dividend plus a first-ever buyback. This is a cash-return story at the wrong price for a 15% hurdle, not a broken business. Leadership is also in transition (Per Narvinger succeeded Börje Ekholm as President and CEO, Ekholm's retirement effective September 30, 2026) — execution continuity is a watch item, not yet a flag.
- Hurdle math: the stock clears 15% (weighted) at the weighted IV@15% of **$7.75**; with a margin of safety against the bear case (IV@15% $5.41), a buyer wanting insurance needs the low-$6s. At $9.58 it clears ~12% at the 12% discount column (IV@12% $10.23) — a C-tier return profile.
